name: Ajanta Caves (Ancient Buddhist Frescoes)
best_time: October to March or during monsoon for lush green gorge and waterfalls
rules: Flash photography and tripods strictly prohibited to preserve ancient vegetable dye frescoes
Eco-friendly electric shuttle bus transports visitors from T-Point parking to cave base
visual_features: horseshoe-shaped volcanic rock ravine hugging thirty ancient rock-cut Buddhist chaitya halls and viharas with carved columned porticoes
description: The Ajanta Caves are 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments dating from the second century BCE to about 480 CE in Aurangabad district of Maharashtra state in India. Ajanta Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Universally regarded as masterpieces of Buddhist religious art, the caves include paintings and rock-cut sculptures, described as among the finest surviving examples of ancient Indian art, particularly expressive paintings that present emotions through gesture, pose and form.
